body:
Every ticket needs a boundary before work starts, and today every one is written by hand. That holds for a couple of items and not for a sprint.

Problem: producing a boundary is manual every time, so the practice lasts only while someone has the patience for it.

Goal: a person receives a drafted boundary built from the refined criteria, and decides whether it freezes.

## Acceptance criteria

AC1. When the refined criteria become ready, a person is asked whether to draft the boundary, and nothing is drafted until they agree. The person is asked once per item; later drafts for the same item do not ask again.

AC2. A reviewer given a drafted boundary names no entry they had to write themselves.

AC3. Refined criteria the drafter cannot produce a boundary from leave the issue recording each missing thing separately, and no boundary is produced.

AC4. Each recorded blocker names the missing criterion or the undecided question, and can be resolved without resolving the others.

AC5. Resolving the last blocker produces a new drafted boundary without anyone being asked again.

AC6. A boundary written or edited by hand freezes without any step a drafted one does not require.

AC7. Every frozen boundary carries a recorded approval by a person, recorded at the freeze. Approval at merge is a different gate and does not satisfy this one.

## Out of scope

- Reducing how much a person reviews. Separate item, blocked on measuring what review costs.
- The boundary's shape. It may change to suit the agent stage; this item neither requires nor prevents that.
- Producing the refined criteria. That is the upstream stage.
title: Draft the boundary from the refined criteria
